Hi Soojin —

Thanks for the onboarding call this morning. Per our procurement checklist, attached is MerchantLayer's redline of Redwood's standard DPA (MerchantLayer_DPA_redline_v3.pdf) and our SCCs annex (SCCs_Annex_MerchantLayer.docx). A few high-level asks so we can close legal review: 

- Can you confirm Redwood's default data retention for customer transactional logs and whether you can support a 2-year retention maximum for this account?
- MerchantLayer needs SOC 2 Type II or an AICPA SIG completed within the last 12 months; if you only provide SOC 2, please point us to the secure download link.
- We have a HIPAA carve-in for one of our merchant verticals — please confirm whether Redwood will sign HIPAA terms (Business Associate Addendum) and provide evidence of relevant controls.
- We requested clarity on subprocessor list and notification cadence for changes.

From a timeline perspective, our procurement lead would like legal-ready redlines within 4 business days. I attached our redlines inline; please let me know the best contact on your side to iterate.

Thanks —
Karen Rivers
Sr. Counsel, MerchantLayer

Thanks, Soojin — reviewed MerchantLayer's redline and SCCs annex. High-level notes and proposed path: 

- SOC 2 / SIG: We can provide the SOC 2 Type II report under NDA; I will upload the latest report to the secure folder and share a time-limited link (see Drive link below). If they need a completed SIG, we can provide Part A answers within 3 business days and then coordinate Part B with their security team.

- Retention: MerchantLayer's 2-year retention ask conflicts with our standard 5-year retention for transaction logs. Commercially, a 2-year cap is feasible only if the deal value and commit justify it (it impacts backup/restore and analytics retention). Marissa / Karthik, please confirm whether Revenue is willing to accept a 2-year retention for this account or if we should offer a compromise (e.g., 3 years + archival access on request).

- HIPAA / BAA: We will sign a BAA for Hosted API customers when the use of Protected Health Information is confirmed. We need the customer to identify the specific data classes that will be PHI. Operationally, we'll need to validate deployed safeguards (encryption at rest, access controls, logging). I attached our draft counterproposal (RI_DPA_counterproposal_v1.docx) that keeps standard Redwood protections, accepts SCCs annex with a limited data residency statement, and proposes a 30-day notification window for subprocessors.

- Subprocessors & SCCs: We propose to accept the SCCs annex with a minor amendment: replace an open transfer clause with a reference to our published subprocessor list and monthly notification cadence. This keeps us operationally simple and gives the customer the visibility they need.

Next steps I recommend: 
1) Share the SOC 2 secure link and offer SIG Part A answers by 3/26.
2) Sales (So): confirm commercial willingness on retention. If Sales approves 2-year retention, Legal will accept the limited retention clause. If not, propose a 3-year compromise.
3) If HIPAA is material, Customer must complete a short questionnaire identifying PHI flows; we can then sign a BAA with standard Rider.

I will upload the SOC 2 under NDA and circulate RI_DPA_counterproposal_v1.docx for internal sign-off.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai

Attachments: RI_DPA_counterproposal_v1.docx
